newsitem.title: UK: Italy French franc benchmark Eurobond a success.
newsitem.headline: Italy French franc benchmark Eurobond a success.

text.p: Italy launched its first-ever French franc Eurobond on Wednesday, setting another well-received benchmark bond in a key European currency, bankers said.
"We have roughly sold out of paper," an official at J.P. Morgan, joint lead manager of the deal, said.
"It was a real success, and Italy has set a benchmark in the French franc sector," he said.
The five billion French franc ($862 million) 10-year Eurobond was priced to yield 18 basis points over French government bonds, OATs.

"The size, maturity and price are absolutely correct. The size will provide a lot of liquidity, the spread is fair and is expected to tighten, and 10 years is the benchmark maturity in the French market," the J.P. Morgan official said.
Bankers at rival banks were also positive.
"We have seen a lot of interest in the bond, and placed paper with French buyers and in Italy too," a Paris-based Eurobond specialist said.
"The deal is trading at the reoffer price -- its a very good deal," he said.
The bond is a latest in a series of benchmark transactions Italy has issued in key European currencies, as part of a drive to familiarise European investors with its credit ahead of monetary union.
"Italy wants to create a benchmark is all the major European currencies," the J.P. Morgan official said. "It has already tapped guilders, Swiss francs and Ecu so French francs was the next step."
He said around one third of Wednesday's bond was sold outside France, with the rest bought by French life insurance companies and mutual funds.
Last week Italy issued a one billion Swiss franc seven-year bond, in May it launched a 1.25 billion guilder 15-year bond and in March a one billion Ecu-into-euro seven-year bond.
All its deals, apart from the Swiss franc transaction, have clauses which allow for the redenomination into the euro.
Italy is keen to be among the first countries to adopt the euro, scheduled to be introduced on January 1, 1999, although the timetable has come under question in recent weeks.

Since the start of this year, regular Euromarket borrowers have been launching euro-related bonds or benchmark deals in key European currencies in preparation for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
As currency risks are eliminated, investors are expected to buy a wider range of credits and competition between borrowers will heat up.
-- Aline van Duyn, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7748 ($ = 5.8 French Francs)
